title: Eleven Acres and One Drought
subtitle: 农作物与收成 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 农作物与收成（自然生态·植物与农业）
meta: 主题语境：农作物与收成（自然生态·植物与农业）　|　核心词汇：crop　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 crop 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 my grandfather ① lost a crop to a drought that came in the eleventh week, and he said the losing was the whole of the year. The ② crop, meaning the harvest and not the field, filled eleven acres and stayed that size in the account; crop, he said, is the only thing in a summer that is judged by how much of it never comes.

Every ③ crop in that valley had the same sowing day, and the ④ crop at the end, meaning the one he kept for the seed and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever weighed twice. Crop, my grandmother said, is nine parts sowing day and one part somebody willing to wait; my grandfather said the waiting is the part that fills eleven acres.

My mother meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the crop was the whole of the photograph, meaning the cutting off and not the harvest. The ⑥ crop, meaning the cutting off and not any of that, is the only thing in a photograph that everybody notices and nobody asks about; crop, she said, is either something you lose or the only word that means both a harvest and a cutting off. He said the cutting off is the part they remember.

By 1960 the ⑦ crop had become a line in a return, and the return had become an argument about the sowing day. The ⑧ crop of the whole thing, my grandfather wrote in August, was one drought and thirty years of waiting; crop, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to wait. She said the waiting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ crop I remember is the one at the end, which he saved in 1966 and is still described as the smallest in the county. A ⑩ crop, my grandmother said in 1968, is the only thing that improves by being waited for; every crop, she said, is a cutting off that has agreed to look like a harvest. She said the cutting off was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 收成（指那次收获本身，与那片田地相对）
C. 固定搭配：lose a crop 损失一季收成
D. n. 庄稼（指那个山谷里每一季）
E. n. 收成（指末尾那一季）
F. n. 剪裁；裁切（指照片的裁切）
G. n. 收成（指报表里提到的那一季）
H. n. 作物；一季收成（抽象总称）

items.q: lost a crop to a drought that came in the eleventh week
The crop, meaning the harvest and not the field
the crop was the whole of the photograph
The crop, meaning the cutting off
the crop had become a line in a return
The crop of the whole thing
A crop, my grandmother said in 1968

answers.why: lose a crop 意为“损失一季收成”，1952 年祖父因一场在第十一周到来的旱灾损失了一季收成。
crop 意为“收成”，指那次收获本身而不是那片田地，占十一英亩。
crop 指那个山谷里每一季庄稼，每一季都在同一天下种。
crop 指末尾那一季（他留作种子的那一季），是唯一有人称过两次的。
crop 意为“剪裁、裁切”，母亲说裁切就是那张照片的全部，指的是照片的裁切而不是那次收获。
crop 为摄影用语，指照片的裁切而不是那次收获，是照片里人人都注意到、却无人过问的东西。
crop 意为“收成”，指报表里提到的那一季，到 1960 年这季收成成了报表里的一行。
crop 意为“作物、一季收成”，祖父八月写道，整件事的收成是一场旱灾三十年的等待。
crop 意为“庄稼、收成”，我记得的是末尾那一季，他 1966 年留种，至今仍被说成全县最小的。
crop 为抽象总称，祖母说一季收成是唯一会因为被等待而变好的东西。
